title: Residue-linear lift of evaluated simultaneous reduction arrows
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $W$ any scheme, and $D$ a simultaneous derived reduction of scalar extension from abelian pro-etale sheaves to constant $\mathbf Z_\ell$-module sheaves [def-sfb-diagonal-system-interface], with the small Ext conventions [lem-sfb-canonical-sheaf-ext]. Let $M,S$ be arbitrary abelian sheaves, $H$ a strict p-adic module system, and $b:D.T(M[1])\simeq H[2]$. Fix a level $n$ (exponent $n+1$) and residue-module sheaves $P,Q$. Write $F_n$ for restriction from $\mathbf Z/\ell^{n+1}$ to $\mathbf Z_\ell$. Let $t:H_n\simeq F_nP$, let $a:D.T(S[0])\simeq D.ordinary(S)[0]$ have hom equal to the canonical derived counit, and let $s:D.ordinary(S)_n\simeq F_nQ$. Then for every $f\in\operatorname{Ext}^1(S,M)$ there is $e\in\operatorname{Ext}^2(Q,P)$ whose exact-functor image under $F_n$ is evaluation of $a^{-1}D.T(f)b$, precomposed with $s^{-1}$ and postcomposed with $t$. This asserts lifting only for these derived-reduction arrows, not fullness of coefficient restriction on arbitrary Ext groups. There is no Kummer assumption, roots object, invertibility hypothesis on $\ell$ on $W$, or scalar-adjunct formula.

source.place: Step (2), computation by one K-flat resolution, and step (4), evaluation through residue extension before scalar restriction; arbitrary source and target identifications.

proof.text: The evaluated derived-reduction functor factors through the derived category of residue-module sheaves by [lem-sfb-diagonal-residue-derived-factorization].

Restriction along the surjective coefficient projection is exact, full and faithful on sheaves. It reflects cohomological concentration. A derived object whose restriction is isomorphic to a single-degree object is therefore itself concentrated in that degree. Express both objects as single-degree objects; fullness and faithfulness on sheaves lift the prescribed isomorphism. Apply this argument at degree zero to the source and at degree minus two to the target.

Apply the residue derived functor to f and conjugate by these two lifted isomorphisms. Use the Ext/Hom equivalence to define e. The naturality square of the factorization isomorphism, together with the exact-functor single and shift comparisons, proves the required equality of Ext classes.
